title: The Community Garden
author: Barashada Ingiriisiga
description: Neighbours from different countries turn a small empty garden into a shared vegetable patch, work together to fix a water problem, and celebrate with a harvest meal that brings everyone closer.

chapters.title: The Empty Garden
chapters.text:
The sun was warm on the small street. Maria looked out of her kitchen window. She saw the empty garden behind the apartment building. It was a sad place. Old leaves and dry grass covered the ground. No flowers grew there. No vegetables. Nothing.

Maria lived in apartment three. Her family was from Mexico. Next door, in apartment four, lived the Chen family. They were from China. In apartment one, Mr. and Mrs. Silva lived. They were from Brazil. And in apartment two, a young man named Ahmed lived. He was from Egypt.

That evening, Maria went outside. She walked to the empty garden. She looked at the dry ground and thought. Soon, Ahmed came out too. He smiled at Maria.

"This garden is very sad," Maria said.

"Yes," Ahmed said. "It is a big space. But we do not use it."

Then the Chen family came out. Mrs. Chen had a small bag of seeds in her hand. "We want to plant something," she said. "But where?"

Mr. Silva walked over too. He looked at the garden. "My father had a garden in Brazil," he said. "He grew many things. I can help."

Maria had an idea. "We can make a community garden," she said. "All of us together. We can plant vegetables from our countries."

Mrs. Chen smiled. "A good idea. We can plant Chinese cabbage."

"I want to plant tomatoes," Maria said. "My grandmother grew the best tomatoes in Mexico."

"I can plant peppers," Mr. Silva said. "Hot peppers from Brazil."

"And I will plant mint," Ahmed said. "For tea. My mother always had mint in her garden."

So the neighbours made a plan. The next Saturday, they all came out with tools. Ahmed had an old shovel. Maria found a rake. The Chen family brought a watering can. Mr. Silva had strong hands and a big smile.

They worked all morning. They pulled the old weeds from the ground. They turned the soil with the shovel. It was hard work, but they worked together. The children helped too. They carried small stones away from the garden.

The sun was high when they finished. The ground was soft and brown. It was ready. They made four small squares in the soil. In each square, they planted different seeds. Maria put her tomato seeds in one square. Mrs. Chen planted her cabbage in another. Mr. Silva made a small hole for his pepper seeds. And Ahmed planted his mint in the corner.

Then Maria brought water from her house. She poured it slowly on the new seeds. Everyone watched.

"Now we wait," Maria said.

"Yes," Mr. Silva said. "And we hope."

They all looked at the small garden. It was not empty anymore. It was full of dreams.

chapters.title: The Water Problem
chapters.text:
The sun was very hot that week. It did not rain for seven days. The small plants in the garden were not happy. Their leaves were yellow and dry. The tomatoes looked sad. The beans did not grow. The children looked at the plants and felt worried.

Maria touched the soil. It was hard and dry, like old bread. "The plants need water," she said. "But there is no rain."

Mr. Chen looked at his long green beans. "We use water from our houses for the kitchen and the bathroom. We cannot use all of it for the garden."

The neighbours were sad. They worked hard to make the garden. Now the plants were dying.

That evening, all the neighbours met in the garden. They sat on old chairs and boxes. The sun was going down, but the air was still hot.

"We need a plan," said Fatima. She had a small baby and she spoke with a quiet voice. "The plants are thirsty."

"We can carry water from the river," said Tom. "But the river is very far. It is too much work."

"We can buy water from the shop," said Anna. "But it costs too much money."

Then Mr. Chen had an idea. He looked at the roof of the building. "Look at the roof," he said. "When it rains, the water falls from the roof to the ground. It goes away. But we can catch it!"

The neighbours looked at the roof. It was big and flat.

"Yes!" said Maria. "We can make a rain collector. We can use old pipes and barrels."

The next day, everyone worked together. Tom found some old pipes in his garage. Mr. Chen had two big blue barrels. Fatima's husband made a small hole in the bottom of each barrel.

They put the barrels under the roof. They put the pipes from the roof to the barrels. When it rained, the water would go from the roof, through the pipes, and into the barrels.

It was hard work. The sun was hot. But they laughed and talked. The children helped too. They carried small tools and brought cold water for the workers.

After two days, the rain collector was ready. But the sky was still blue. There was no rain.

"We need to wait," said Tom.

The neighbours waited. They looked at the sky every morning. They looked at the dry plants.

Then, on the third day, the sky became grey. Dark clouds came. The wind started to blow.

"Rain is coming!" shouted the children.

And the rain came. It fell on the roof. It went through the pipes. It fell into the barrels. Drip, drip, drip. The barrels started to fill with clean, fresh water.

The neighbours were very happy. They used the water from the barrels for the plants. They shared the water fairly. Each family had a turn. The plants drank the water and stood up tall again.

The garden was safe. And the neighbours learned that when they worked together, they could solve any problem.

chapters.title: The Harvest Meal
chapters.text:
The summer passed, and the garden grew full and green. Every day, the neighbours came to look at their plants. They watered them with the rain collector. They pulled out the small weeds. They watched the vegetables grow bigger and bigger.

One morning, Maria looked at the big red tomatoes. She smiled. "Look!" she said. "The tomatoes are ready. It is time to pick them."

The other neighbours came out of their houses. They brought baskets and bags. They walked between the rows of plants. They picked the long green cucumbers. They pulled the orange carrots from the soft earth. They cut the big green leaves of the lettuce. They picked the round red peppers and the small yellow onions.

The children helped too. They carried the baskets to the big table in the middle of the garden. The table was full of beautiful vegetables. The colours were bright and happy.

"Now we must cook!" said Mr. Chen. "Everyone brings a dish from their country."

The neighbours went to their homes. The kitchen windows opened. The smells came out into the garden. There were many good smells.

Maria made a big pot of tomato soup. She put fresh tomatoes, onions, and small pieces of bread in it. It was red and warm.

Mr. Chen made fried rice with carrots and peppers. He moved the food fast in the hot pan. The rice was yellow and shiny.

Mrs. Patel made a dish with potatoes and many spices. It was orange and smelled very strong and good.

The young woman from Mexico made fresh salsa. She cut the tomatoes and onions into small pieces. She added green pepper and a little lemon. It was fresh and bright.

The man from Italy made pasta. He cooked the long noodles and put fresh tomato sauce on top. He added green leaves from the garden.

When the sun went down, they put all the food on the long table. There was a lot of food. The neighbours sat on chairs and benches around the table. The lights from the houses made the garden warm and soft.

They ate and talked. They laughed at funny stories. The children ran between the tables. They tasted food from many countries.

"This tomato soup is so good," said Mrs. Patel.

"Thank you," said Maria. "The tomatoes are from the garden. We all grew them together."

"Yes," said Mr. Chen. "We worked together. We built the rain collector together. And now we eat together."

They looked at the empty plates. They looked at each other. They were tired but happy.

"This is a good garden," said the man from Italy. "And we are good neighbours."

They cleaned the tables together. They washed the dishes together. Then they went home, one by one. The garden was quiet and dark. But in the morning, the vegetables would grow again. And the neighbours would come back to the garden, together.
